record.context_brief: Representation-theoretic route to stronger lower bounds
record.original_question: Can one prove a lower bound for computing X_alpha in the same two-coordinate unitary-step model that is stronger than Omega(alpha n log n), possibly by choosing a nontrivial unitary representation Psi of U(n), composing the entropy-style potential Phi with Psi, and in particular exploiting the order-k determinant representation Psi_det^k(U) whose (I, J) entry is det U_{I,J}?

evidence.quote: Is it possible to get a stronger lower bound than alpha n log n? One approach for solving this problem might be using group representation theory.
If Psi : U(n) -> U(n') is any unitary representation of U(n), then we could define a new potential function Phi o Psi on U(n), and use it to obtain possibly better lower bounds.
So far I have not been able to make progress on the problem using this (quite natural) representation, but I am not convinced that this direction is futile either.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix an integer n ≥ 2. Consider the computational model in which a linear operator on ℂ^n is built by composing a sequence of "two-coordinate unitary steps": each step is a unitary U_t ∈ U(n) that acts as the identity on all but two coordinates i_t, j_t, and acts as an arbitrary 2×2 unitary on the (i_t, j_t)-block. The complexity of computing a target unitary X ∈ U(n) is the minimum number T of such steps needed so that the composition U_T ⋯ U_1 equals X (or, in approximate versions, lies within a prescribed neighborhood of X).

For a unitary U ∈ U(n), define the matrix-entropy potential
   Φ(U) = − Σ_{i,j} |U_{i,j}|^2 · log |U_{i,j}|^2 ,
with the convention 0·log 0 = 0. A single two-coordinate step can change Φ by at most O(1), and this is the key ingredient that yields the known lower bound Ω(α n log n) for computing a family of target unitaries {X_α}_{α∈(0,1]} associated with the (suitably normalized) discrete Fourier transform on ℂ^n, where α encodes a quality/precision parameter (so that α = 1 corresponds to exact computation of the Fourier transform).

Representation-theoretic approach. Let Ψ : U(n) → U(n′) be any (continuous) unitary representation of U(n). Then the composed potential Φ ∘ Ψ : U(n) → ℝ is also a candidate progress measure for the same two-coordinate model. A natural example is the order-k determinant representation Ψ_{det}^{k} : U(n) → U( C(n,k) ), whose rows and columns are indexed by k-subsets I, J ⊆ {1,…,n} and whose (I, J) entry is det U_{I,J}, the determinant of the k×k submatrix of U with rows I and columns J.

Problem. Prove a lower bound on the number of two-coordinate unitary steps required to compute X_α (in the model above) that is asymptotically stronger than Ω(α n log n). In particular, decide whether choosing a non-trivial unitary representation Ψ of U(n) — for instance Ψ = Ψ_{det}^{k} for some 1 < k < n — and using the composed potential Φ ∘ Ψ as a progress measure can be made to yield such an improved lower bound.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem was explicitly posed as an open problem by Ailon in 2019, who reports being unable to make progress with the determinant representation. No subsequent work was found that achieves a lower bound asymptotically stronger than Ω(α n log n) in the two-coordinate unitary-step model via this representation-theoretic route; it appears to remain open as of the current search.

status_evidence.title: Interesting Open Problem Related to Complexity of Computing the Fourier Transform and Group Theory
status_evidence.snippet: the goal of this document is to describe a natural open problem that arises from this work, which is related to group theory, and in particular to representation theory
status_evidence.claim: Author frames the strengthening of the Ω(n log n) bound via representation theory as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: A Lower Bound for Fourier Transform Computation in a Linear Model Over 2x2 Unitary Gates Using Matrix Entropy
status_evidence.snippet: Ω(n log n) bound for computing the normalized Fourier Transform assuming only unitary operations on pairs of coordinates is allowed
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the baseline Ω(n log n) bound that the open problem seeks to strengthen.
